title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Woolworths Team Members
tiers.description: Each director and officer of Woolworths Group and its subsidiaries, all employees wherever based, and contractors and consultants whose engagement terms apply the Policy. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, the short-term and speculative trading ban (including short selling) and the ban on Derivatives over unvested or restricted Woolworths Securities.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: Woolworths Group Directors, Subsidiary directors and company secretaries, members of the Executive (Group Executive Committee and direct reports to the CEO), direct reports to members of the Executive, General Managers and key 'Heads of', and Team Members designated in writing. Subject to Blackout Periods, prior written clearance for any Trade at any time, the collateral ban and the hedging clearance requirement, all extended to Closely Related Parties.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board (Chair)
tiers.description: Sub-tier of Specified Persons for clearance: endorsed by CEO, CLO and Company Secretary, approved by the Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee.

tiers.name: Woolworths Group Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Woolworths Group Limited (other than the Chair) for clearance purposes: endorsed by CEO, CLO and Company Secretary, approved by the Chair. Also subject to the two-day post-trade notification, HIN/SRN provision, Listing Rule notifiable interest disclosure and discretionary public disclosure of Derivative positions.

tiers.name: CEO
tiers.description: Chief Executive Officer: endorsed by CLO and Company Secretary, approved by the Chair. Subject to the Executive post-trade notification and Minimum Shareholding Policy monitoring.

tiers.name: Chief Legal Officer (CLO)
tiers.description: Chief Legal Officer: endorsed by CEO and Company Secretary, approved by the Chair.

tiers.name: Executives, Subsidiary Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Group Executive Committee, other direct reports to the CEO, and Subsidiary directors: endorsed by CLO and Company Secretary, approved by the CEO. Executives are also subject to the two-day post-trade notification and Minimum Shareholding Policy monitoring.

tiers.name: All other Specified Persons
tiers.description: Specified Persons below Executive level (direct reports to the Executive, General Managers, key Heads of, designated roles): approved by the Company Secretary or CLO with no endorsers.

tiers.name: Closely Related Parties
tiers.description: Family members (including spouse and dependent children), family companies where the Specified Person is a director and/or shareholder, and family trusts or superannuation funds where the Specified Person is a trustee, beneficiary or an advisor to the trustee. The Specified Person must make the clearance request on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

before market open on the business day following release to ASX of the Full Year financial results

before market open on the business day following release to ASX of the Quarter 3 sales results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, on recommendation of the Chief Legal Officer or Company Secretary, may vary the Blackout Periods or impose a restriction on Trading during other periods where deemed appropriate. Confidentiality of such restrictions is not addressed.

rules.detail: All Team Members are barred from using any Derivative (s761D derivatives including options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars, and any risk-limiting transaction) in relation to unvested Woolworths Securities. No approval route.
rules.evidence: Woolworths Team Members must not use any Derivatives in relation to any unvested Woolworths Securities or vested Woolworths Securities that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: The same ban applies to vested Woolworths Securities still subject to disposal restrictions.
rules.evidence: or vested Woolworths Securities that are still subject to disposal restrictions

rules.detail: Derivatives (expressly including options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars, with no venue limit) are Securities, so entering one is a Trade requiring prior written clearance under Schedule 1 at any time, valid five business days, and barred in Blackout Periods. Section 4.1 expressly requires clearance for hedging arrangements over vested and unrestricted Securities. Director Derivative positions may be publicly disclosed by Woolworths.
rules.evidence: enter into hedging arrangements in relation to vested and unrestricted Woolworths Securities (no hedging) without first obtaining clearance in accordance with section 4.3.

rules.detail: Team Members who are not Specified Persons need no clearance and face no hedging restriction over vested, unrestricted Securities; they remain subject to the insider trading prohibition, the front page test and the speculative and short-term trading bans.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy (outlined in section 4) only apply to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties.

rules.detail: Because Derivative includes any transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of holding the securities, section 3.4 is a hedging ban over unvested Securities for all Team Members.
rules.evidence: The use of Derivatives in this way can have the effect of distorting the proper functioning of these hurdles and reduce the intended alignment with shareholders' interests.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities still subject to disposal restrictions is banned for all Team Members.
rules.evidence: Woolworths Team Members must not use any Derivatives in relation to any unvested Woolworths Securities or vested Woolworths Securities that are still subject to disposal restrictions.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested and unrestricted Woolworths Securities is permitted for Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties only with prior written clearance from the Schedule 1 approver; the parenthetical '(no hedging)' signals the default expectation but the operative text is a clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: enter into hedging arrangements in relation to vested and unrestricted Woolworths Securities (no hedging) without first obtaining clearance in accordance with section 4.3.

rules.detail: No hedging restriction applies to non-Specified Team Members once Securities have vested and are free of disposal restrictions.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy (outlined in section 4) only apply to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties.

rules.detail: Collars, forward contracts and swaps are named as Derivatives, so the option legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are a clearable hedging arrangement. The loan leg is separately prohibited by the collateral ban, so only an unfunded collar is achievable.
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: Short selling is named as an example of speculative Trading and banned for all Team Members.
rules.evidence: Woolworths Team Members are also not permitted to Trade in Woolworths Securities on a speculative basis (including short selling).

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named. A loan of shares involves a change in beneficial ownership and an agreement to deal, so it is a Trade requiring clearance for Specified Persons; lending to facilitate short selling would offend the speculative trading ban.
rules.evidence: engaging in any transaction involving a change in beneficial ownership of the Securities, or the entry into any agreement to do any of the above things

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are s761D derivatives and so Securities; a CFD is a Trade requiring clearance and, being typically short-term or speculative (or short), would in practice fall foul of section 3.3. CFDs over unvested or restricted Securities are banned by 3.4.
rules.evidence: Woolworths Team Members are also not permitted to Trade in Woolworths Securities on a speculative basis (including short selling).

rules.detail: No new margin lending arrangements following the date of the Policy (20 August 2021) for Specified Persons and Closely Related Parties; pre-existing arrangements are not addressed and appear grandfathered.
rules.evidence: enter into arrangements to use Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction following the date of this Policy (no new margin lending arrangements)

rules.detail: The collateral ban is in section 4, which applies only to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties; other Team Members are not restricted.
rules.evidence: Certain aspects of this Policy (outlined in section 4) only apply to Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties.

rules.detail: Using Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction is banned. Creating any security interest or other financial interest over Securities is also a Trade, so an encumbrance outside a financial transaction would still need clearance and be barred in Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: Trade, Trading includes buying, selling or otherwise dealing in Securities, including creating a security interest or other financial interest over Securities

rules.detail: Ban on any new arrangement using Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, not limited to margin loans; no vesting-state, tier or approval carve-out and no exemption authority.
rules.evidence: enter into arrangements to use Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction following the date of this Policy

rules.detail: Non-Specified Team Members are not subject to the collateral ban.
rules.evidence: Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties are subject to additional Trading restrictions and must not:

rules.detail: Three-month holding period from purchase, with a carve-out for sales within 3 months of vesting or release from restriction under an employee share scheme; separate ban on speculative Trading.
rules.evidence: Woolworths Team Members must not sell Woolworths Securities within 3 months after their purchase except for the sale of Woolworths Securities within 3 months of their vesting or release from restrictions under a Woolworths employee share scheme.

financing_disclosure: Woolworths Group Directors and Executives: notify the Company Secretary of any Trading (which includes creating a security interest over Securities) as soon as practicable and no more than two days afterward, and provide HIN/SRN for all relevant holdings (4.5).

Woolworths Group Directors: Woolworths may publicly disclose any Derivative positions over Woolworths Securities taken out by a Director, whether or not technically required by the Listing Rules or Corporations Act (4.5).
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Woolworths monitors Directors' and Executives' compliance with the Woolworths Group Minimum Shareholding Policy (where applicable); the Trading Policy does not say whether hedged or encumbered shares count toward it.

exemption_authority: The Schedule 1 approver may grant clearance to dispose of (not acquire) Woolworths Securities in a Blackout Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, final court order or regulatory undertaking, or other exceptional circumstance) where disposal is the only reasonable option and the person holds no Inside Information. The Board, on recommendation of the CLO or Company Secretary, may vary Blackout Periods. No authority is given to waive the collateral ban, the Derivatives-over-unvested ban or the short-term trading rule.
jurisdiction_overlays: Policy and insider trading prohibitions apply to Trading inside and outside Australia (2.3)

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into arrangements to use Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction following the date of this Policy (no new margin lending arrangements)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is a new arrangement using Woolworths Securities as collateral and is prohibited for Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties, so only an unfunded collar is available; the ban is prospective, so pre-20 August 2021 facilities appear grandfathered.

bespoke_clauses.clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is expressly a Derivative and therefore a Security and a Trade, so it is squarely within the clearance, Blackout Period and section 3.4 regimes regardless of OTC form.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into hedging arrangements in relation to vested and unrestricted Woolworths Securities (no hedging) without first obtaining clearance in accordance with section 4.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The option legs over vested unrestricted shares are permissible with prior written clearance, although the '(no hedging)' label signals approvers may be reluctant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trade, Trading includes ... creating a security interest or other financial interest over Securities, engaging in any transaction involving a change in beneficial ownership of the Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting security to the bank or transferring shares to a custodian or the bank would itself be a Trade needing clearance and barred in Blackout Periods, in addition to the collateral ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Specified Person, or any Closely Related Party to a Specified Person, who wishes to trade in Woolworths Securities at any time must seek prior approval in writing from the relevant approver in Schedule 1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance is required outside Blackout Periods too, so inception, roll, unwind and physical settlement of the collar each need fresh written clearance valid for five business days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Woolworths may also publicly disclose any Derivative positions over Woolworths Securities taken out by a Woolworths Group Director. These disclosures may be made irrespective of whether or not they are technically required by the ASX Listing Rules or the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director's collar may be announced to the market at Woolworths' discretion even where no Appendix 3Y obligation arises.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Provided a Trade is placed and executed by you or your broker prior to the commencement of a Blackout Period, it is not a breach of this Policy if the Trade settles and clears after the commencement of a Blackout Period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar executed before a Blackout Period may settle inside it, but option expiry or exercise falling within a Blackout Period is not covered by this relief.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Trade in Woolworths Securities during designated Blackout Periods (closed periods)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no carve-out for a lender's or counterparty's enforcement or physical settlement in a Blackout Period, and the hardship exception requires clearance and a demonstrated absence of any other reasonable option.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Woolworths Team Members must not sell Woolworths Securities within 3 months after their purchase
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares bought within the past three months cannot be delivered under the call, and a collar unwound quickly may be characterised as speculative Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: family trusts or superannuation funds where the Specified Person is a trustee, beneficiary or an advisor to the trustee
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family trust, SMSF or family company does not escape the collateral ban or the clearance requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed Trading be perceived by the market as me taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the Trade was reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approvers may apply a reputational filter to an executive collar independent of the technical rules.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for Woolworths Specified Persons (directors, Executives, their direct reports, General Managers and designated roles, together with their Closely Related Parties) because section 4.1 prohibits any new arrangement using Woolworths Securities as collateral in any financial transaction after 20 August 2021, with no approval or exemption route. An unfunded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is achievable: collars are expressly Derivatives and hedging of vested unrestricted Securities is permitted with prior written clearance from the Schedule 1 approver (Chair of the Audit and Finance Committee for the Chair; Chair for directors, CEO and CLO; CEO for Executives; Company Secretary or CLO for others), valid five business days, outside the four Blackout Periods running from the 20th of the last month of each quarter. Derivatives over unvested or disposal-restricted Securities are banned for all Team Members, shares cannot be sold within three months of purchase, creating a security interest is itself a Trade, and Directors' and Executives' trades must be reported to the Company Secretary within two days, with Woolworths free to publicly disclose a Director's Derivative positions.
